summary: Opaque 34MB Go binary masquerading as a small C sudoku solver, auto-executed at install
details: The npm package @workoscalifant/sudoku-term@1.1.7 ships prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint (33,976,468 bytes, sha256 ac6b4523fbe02c79129e58bdc8d613ddfb3a786c23dd03fa4ab28ab38ff3e6e5) and executes it during install via scripts/postinstall.js, which calls execFileSync(bin, ['--selftest'], { timeout: 5000 }). The README documents this file as a ~26 KB static-musl ELF compiled from the shipped ~200-line C source native/hint.c using gcc on Alpine, and states it 'reads no files, opens no sockets'. The shipped darwin-x64 prebuilt (12,968 bytes, Mach-O) is consistent with that C source, but the linux-x64 prebuilt is a ~34 MB Go binary containing Go runtime/reflection/scheduler symbols (runtime., GODEBUG=, reflect., godebugs.Info, chacha8:, [bisect-, memprofile) and Linux introspection paths (/proc/self/, /proc/self/mountinfo, /proc/self/cgroup) that cannot be produced by the documented C toolchain and is roughly 1,300x the documented size. The Linux binary's actual behavior cannot be verified from the shipped sources, and it is invoked automatically on every linux-x64 npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
